response.sql:
WITH cnt AS (
  SELECT o.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM `order` o
  JOIN disp dp ON dp.account_id = o.account_id AND dp.type = 'OWNER'
  JOIN client c ON c.client_id = dp.client_id
  JOIN district d ON d.district_id = c.district_id
  GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3
),
diffs AS (
  SELECT account_id, region, order_count,
         order_count - AVG(order_count) OVER () AS diff_from_avg
  FROM cnt
),
reg AS (
  SELECT account_id, region, order_count, diff_from_avg,
         AVG(diff_from_avg) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_avg_diff
  FROM diffs
)
SELECT account_id, region, order_count, diff_from_avg,
       diff_from_avg - region_avg_diff AS excess_over_region_avg
FROM reg
WHERE diff_from_avg > region_avg_diff
ORDER BY excess_over_region_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Each account has a single OWNER disposition, so an account appears in one account–region row; the overall average is taken over these rows (accounts having at least one order).
Ties at the 10th place are broken arbitrarily by the database.
